newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dragonfield ends debut at 26 pct premium.
newsitem.headline: Dragonfield ends debut at 26 pct premium.

text.p: Shares of leather garments manufacturer Dragonfield Holdings Ltd ended their trading debut on Thursday at HK$1.26 per share, up 26 percent from the issue price of HK$1.00.
Analysts said profit-taking trimmed gains after the stock surged to a high of HK$1.60 in early trade. Turnover was a moderate at 58.36 million shares worth HK$80.77 million.

"The shares closed just slightly above their day low of HK$1.24," said Tony Yung, research director at Tai Fook Securities. "Some investors might take profit for subscribing Beijing Enterprises, which will start IPO on May 20," he said.
The Beijing city government-backed Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd was expected to issue 150 million shares in its initial public offering from May 20-23.
Market sources had said it was seen lifting the IPO price of its shares to a range of HK$11.50 to HK$12.50 from an initial range of HK$8.00 to HK$9.30 due to the overwhelming response.

Analysts said the prospect of Dragonfield should be brighter than other pure manufacturing firms because its trading business and a sale and distribution network in China could help diversifing risks.
"Sellers turned a bit cautious in late trade after Dragonfield moved down to the current price level, or at price/earnings multiple of about 10 times," one said.
Dragonfield offered 90 million new shares at HK$1.00 each in a public offering in Hong Kong, of which 81 million shares available for public subscription was 67.6 times subscribed.
The issue price represents a P/E multiple of 7.91 times on a proforma fully-diluted basis.

Among other leather garments group, Peking Apparel International Group Ltd is trading at about 18 times P/E, Guangdong Tannery Ltd about 24 times, and China Elegance International Fashion Ltd about 21 times.

Dragonfield planned to use the net proceeds raised from the new issue to expand production facilities, set up showrooms and offices in China and Eastern Europe, and increase processing capacity of the dry cleaning services. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
